questions.question: The northern plain of India is formed of _________.
questions.solution:
• *The Northern Plain* was *formed* *by* the deposits brought in by the three major rivers and their tributaries: the Indus, the Ganga and the Brahmaputra.
 
• *Alluvium* was deposited at the foot–hills of the Himalayas for millions of years.
 
• These deposits are now the fertile *Northern Plains*. *Alluvium* is *soil* or sediments deposited by a river or other running water.

questions.question:
Which of the statements given below are incorrect?

1. The author of the novel 'Dodgers' is Don Winslow.

2. The author of the novel 'Forty Thieves' is Bill Beverly.

3. The author of the novel 'The Corrections' is Thomas Perry
questions.solution: The author of the novel 'Dodgers' is Bill Beverly. The author of the novel 'Forty Thieves' is Thomas Perry. The author of the novel 'The Corrections' is Jonathan Franzen.

questions.question: What type of a body plan does coelenterates, ctenophores and echinoderms have?
questions.solution: Animals can be categorized on the basis of their symmetry. When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called **radial symmetry**. Coelenterates, Ctenophores and Echinoderms have this kind of body plan.

questions.question: Lion, Leopard and Tiger are all species of which genus?
questions.solution: Lion, Leopard and Tiger are all species of the genus Panthera. Panthera is a genus within the *Felidae* family that was named and first described by the German naturalist Oken in 1816. The British taxonomist Pocock revised the classification of this genus in 1916 as comprising the species lion, tiger, *jaguar**,* and leopard on the basis of cranial features.

questions.question: ________ means that the President of India can refer any matter that is of public importance or that which involves interpretation of Constitution to Supreme Court for advice.
questions.solution: Article 143 of the Indian Constitution confers upon the Supreme Court advisory jurisdiction. The President may seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact of public importance on which he thinks it beneficial to obtain such an opinion. On such reference from the President, the Supreme Court, after giving it such hearing as it deems fit, may report to the President its opinion thereon. The opinion is only advisory, which the President is free to follow or not to follow.

questions.question: ___________ is the set of all possible combinations of the two inputs that yield the same maximum possible level of output.
questions.solution: An *isoquant* traces out the *combinations* of any *two* *inputs* which *yield* *the same level of output*. An *isoquant* expresses the *set* of technically efficient processes that *yield the same output*. On the basis of the substitutability of *inputs* it is a curve that illustrates *all possible combinations* of resources that will produce a particular *level of output*.

questions.question: The Arabic work of al-Biruni that gave an account of the subcontinent is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e __**Kitab - Al Hind,**__

 
• In **1017** Al-Biruni traveled to the **Indian subcontinent.**
 
• He authored ***“**Kitab* Tarikh *Al**-**Hind*” (History of India) after exploring the Hindu faith practiced in India**.
 
• Most of the works of **Al-Biruni are in Arabic**.

questions.question: ________ is not a storage device.
questions.solution: Linus is not a storage device. It is the best-known and most-used open source operating system. As an operating system, *Linux* is software that sits underneath all of the other software on a computer, receiving requests from those programs and relaying these requests to the computer's hardware.

questions.question: In which city of India is Dhamek Stupa located?
questions.solution: Dhamek Stupa is a massive Buddhist stupa located at Sarnath, 13 km away from Varanasi in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India.

questions.question: Dara Shikoh was killed in conflict with his brother _________.
questions.solution: On 30th August 1659, Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan's son *Dara Shikoh* was put to *death* by *his* younger *brother* Aurangzeb in the battle of Samugarh.

questions.question: From which of the following, is the GDP of a country not derived from?
questions.solution: GDP of a country is derived from the Agricultural, Industrial and Service sectors. Agriculture includes farming, fishing, and forestry. Industry includes manufacturing, energy production, and construction. Services cover government activities, communications, transportation, finance, and all other private economic activities that do not produce material goods.

questions.question: How many union territories does India have as of June 2017?
questions.solution: At present the total number of states in India is 29 and total number of Union territories in India is 07. The seven current union territories are: Chandigarh, *Dadra* and Nagar Haveli, *Daman and Diu*, *Lakshadweep*, *Puducherry**, **Andaman and Nicobar Islands*, National Capital Territory of Delhi.

questions.question: If the speed of an object moving along a straight line is constant, its motion is said to be _________.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Speed (v): The rate of change of distance is called Speed.

 
 
• Speed = Distance/ Time.
 
• Its unit is m/s or km/hr
 
 
 
• Uniform Speed: The motion in which a body is moving with a constant speed (no acceleration) is called uniform speed motion.
 
• Odometer or odograph: It is a device used to measure the distance travelled by the vehicle.
 
• Speedometer or speed meter: A device used by the vehicle to measure the speed of the vehicle

Explanation:__

__
 
• Uniform motion is defined as the motion of an object in which the object travels in a straight line.
 
• Its velocity remains constant along that line as it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, irrespective of the length of the time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Uniform motion: when an object covers equal distance in the equal time interval of time said to be in uniform motion. Here acceleration is zero.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f888266b06d61365f214addeb6a62a20447697e65f76a78034aa04ae8776083.png] 

 
• Non-Uniform motion: when an object covers unequal distances in the equal time interval of time said to be in non-uniform motion. Here acceleration is non- zero.

questions.question: Magnesium (Mg) + Oxygen (O₂) = ?
questions.solution: **Concept** • When magnesium is heated it reacts with oxygen vigorously producing light and heat. Thus, magnesium reacts with oxygen to form Magnesium oxide. The equation can be written as: • 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO plus heat and light

questions.question: ________ scheme launched by the Central Government is a new crop insurance scheme to boost farming sector in the country.
questions.solution: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna was launched on 18th February 2016 by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. PMFBY provides a comprehensive insurance cover against failure of the crop thus helping in stabilising the income of the farmers. The scheme is being administered by Ministry of Agriculture. 21 states implemented the scheme in Kharif 2016 whereas 23 states and 2 UTs have implemented the scheme in Rabi 2016-17.

questions.question: Who is the winner of 2017 Indian Premier League (Cricket)?
questions.solution: Mumbai Indians beat Rising Pune Supergiant to win IPL 2017. They clinched a record third IPL title with a one-run win over Rising Pune Supergiant at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium, Hyderabad.

questions.question: According to an estimate, almost ___ percent forests have been lost in the tropics, compared to only 1 percent in the temperate region.
questions.solution: According to an estimate, almost 40 percent forests have been lost in the tropics, compared to only 1 percent in the temperate region. There are, however, major differences in the rates of forest depletion in different parts of the world. The area of the temperate and boreal forests has now broadly stabilized. It is the tropical forests that are being so rapidly destroyed.

questions.question: What was Australia's rank in 2016 Human Development Index published by the United Nations Development Programme?
questions.solution: Australia’s HDI value for 2016 is 0.939 which put the country in the ‘very high human development’ category positioning it at 2ⁿd out of 188 countries and territories, only after Norway.

questions.question: The Samjhauta Express runs between Delhi to which city in Pakistan?
questions.solution: The Samjhauta Express commonly called the Friend Express, is a twice-weekly train – Wednesday and Sunday runs between Delhi and Attari in India and Lahore in Pakistan. The word Samjhauta means "agreement", "accord" and "compromise" in both Hindi and Urdu.

questions.question: The strength of a force is usually expressed by its ________.
questions.solution: A force can be larger or smaller than the other force. The strength of a force is expressed by its magnitude. The magnitude of a force is expressed in the SI unit of force called **Newton. 1 Newton** is the force which can make an object of 1 kilogram mass to move at a speed of 1 meter per second. The direction in which a force acts is also to be specified. If the magnitude or direction of the applied force changes the effect produced by force also changes.

questions.question: What is the reaction between an acid and a base called?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The reaction of an acid with a base is called a** neutralisation reaction. **__
 
• The products of this reaction are salt and water.
 
• For example, the reaction of hydrochloric acid(HCl) with sodium hydroxide(NaOH) produces a solution of sodium chloride(NaCl)(salt) and some additional water molecules.

questions.question: Who discovered Proton?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e __**Ernest Rutherford,**__

In 1911 Ernest Rutherford who performed many experiments to explore radioactivity did an experiment in which he discovered that the atom must have a concentrated positive center charge that contains most of the atom's mass. questions.question: __________ are made up of sclerenchymatous cells. These are generally absent in the primary phloem but are found in the secondary phloem.
questions.solution: Phloem conducts food materials to various parts of the plant. Phloem fibres are made up of sclerenchymatous cells. Phloem is composed of four kinds of cells: sieve elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres. Companion cells are present only in angiosperms. Companion cells are absent in pteridophytes and gymnosperms. Phloem fibres are absent in the primary phloem of most of the angiosperms. But they are usually present in the secondary phloem.
